questions.question: How many moons does Saturn now have, making it the planet with the most moons in the Solar System?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**274**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Saturn has “gained” 128 new moons in a groundbreaking discovery by astronomers in Taiwan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Saturn’s new title:** "Moon Champion" with 274 moons.

 
 
• 
 
**Discovery significance:** Saturn surpasses all other planets combined in number of moons.

 
 
• 
 
**Moons discovered:** 128 new moons, primarily small (a few kilometers in size).

 
 
• 
 
**Type of moons:** Irregular moons with elliptical orbits at various angles.

 
 
• 
 
**Formation of irregular moons:** Likely small planets captured by Saturn’s gravity and shattered by collisions.

 
 
• 
 
**Insights into Saturn’s rings:** Irregular moons provide clues about Saturn's rings, which are believed to be fragments from comets, asteroids, and moons torn apart by Saturn’s gravity.

 
 
• 
 
**Naming convention:** Moons are temporarily designated with technical names (e.g., "S/2020 S 27") and await official names from the International Astronomical Union (IAU).

 
 
• 
 
**Saturn's Rings:** Composed mainly of water ice with a minor amount of rocky material.

 
 
• 
 
**Titan:** Largest moon of Saturn, even larger than Mercury and Pluto.

questions.question: Saint Narahari Tirtha statue discovered in Simhachalam Temple. Where is this temple located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Visakhapatnam**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• A **three-foot statue** of **Saint Narahari Tīrtha** was discovered at the **Simhachalam Temple** in **Visakhapatnam**, Andhra Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The statue depicts the saint carrying a script on palm leaves, flanked by devotees with folded hands.
 
• **Saint Narahari Tīrtha** is believed to have been born in **Srikakulam**, previously known as Chikakolu, and was part of an aristocratic family in the **Gajapati empire** (now Odisha).
 
• Epigraphical evidence shows that Narahari Tīrtha helped the **Eastern Ganga dynasty** for around **three decades**, implying he was already ordained into the fourth order by **Acharya Madhva** during that time.
 
• The saint’s role in assisting the empire even after ordination demonstrates **Acharya Madhva’s foresightedness** and his commitment to human welfare.
 
• **Narahari Tīrtha** is considered a **multi-faceted personality**, contributing as an **aristocrat**, **intellectual**, and **devotional poet**.
 
• As an aristocrat, he helped ensure that the **king followed Sanatana Dharma** and established a system for **temple administration**.
 
• Inscriptions in the **Simhachalam** and **Srikurmam temples** document his contributions, including honorific titles like **‘Loka Suraksḥaṇa Ati Nipuṇaḥ’** and **‘Yo Avati Kalinga Bhu Sambhavān’**.
 
• The saint’s extended presence in the region contributed to the spread of **Vaiṣṇavism**, a legacy of **Saint Ramanuja**, in a **non-interfering and secular manner**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narahari Tīrtha** was also a **commentator** on **Acharya Madhva's works**, composing several commentaries, with only four surviving today.
 
• He is credited with being the first to compose **Devaranamas** in **Kannada**.
 
• The saint also propagated two significant **art forms**: **Yakṣagana Bayalaṭa** (a dance-drama from coastal Karnataka) and **Kuchipudi** (a classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh).
 
• After accomplishing his mission, Narahari Tīrtha continued his **study with Acharya Madhva** in **Udupi**, where he may have completed his commentaries.
 
• Upon his death, he was consecrated near **Chakratirtha** at **Hampi** on the banks of the **Tungabhadra River**

questions.question: Lok Sabha passed the Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2025. Which concept does the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 remove?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Waqf by user**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Lok Sabha Passes Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2025.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Amendment Purpose:** The Bill amends the Waqf Act of 1995 to improve the management and transparency of Waqf properties in India.

 
 
• 
 
**Removal of "Waqf by User":** Properties continuously used as Waqf (e.g., mosques) now require official documentation (Waqfnama) to be recognized as Waqf.

 
 
• 
 
**Survey of Properties:** The District Collector or other senior officers will now oversee the survey of Waqf properties, replacing the Survey Commissioner.

 
 
• 
 
**Non-Muslim Representation:** Non-Muslim Chief Executive Officers and members may now be appointed to state-level Waqf Boards.

 
 
• 
 
**Limitation Act (1963):** The Bill makes the Limitation Act applicable to Waqf properties, allowing claims of unlawful possession after 12 years.

 
 
• 
 
**Section 107 Deleted:** The deletion allows the Limitation Act to apply to Waqf properties, enabling claims of adverse possession.

 
 
• 
 
**Government’s Rationale:** The amendments are aimed at addressing loopholes such as title disputes and illegal occupations of Waqf properties.

 
 
• 
 
**Transparency Measures:** The Bill mandates a unified digital listing of Waqf properties to reduce litigation and improve transparency.

 
 
• 
 
**Criticism:** Opposition argues the Bill gives the government too much power over Waqf properties, potentially undermining Muslim community rights.

 
 
• 
 
**Disputed Properties:** The government (through the District Collector) will treat disputed Waqf properties as government property until resolved.

questions.question: Every year, March 23 is observed as Martyrs’ Day as a tribute to freedom fighters Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar, and Shivaram Rajguru. In which year were they executed by the British government?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**1931**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Every year, March 23 is observed as Martyrs’ Day as a tribute to freedom fighters Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar, and Shivaram Rajguru.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Martyrs' Day** or **Shaheed Diwas** is observed every year on **23 March** as a tribute to freedom fighters **Bhagat Singh**, **Sukhdev Thapar**, and **Shivaram Rajguru**.

 
 
• 
 
They were **executed** by the **British government** on this day in **1931** for assassinating **John Saunders**, a British police officer, in **1928**.

 
 
• 
 
They mistook **Saunders** for **James Scott**, the British police superintendent, who had ordered the lathi charge that led to the death of **Lala Lajpat Rai**.

 
 
• 
 
Bhagat Singh and **Batukeshwar Dutt** set off explosives inside the **Central Legislative Assembly** in **Delhi** in **1929**, and shouted the famous slogan: **"Inquilab Zindabad"** ("Long live the revolution").

 
 
• 
 
Martyrs' Day on **30 January** is a separate observance to mark the assassination of **Mahatma Gandhi**.

 
 
• 
 
The actions of **Singh**, **Thapar**, and **Rajguru** have inspired countless youth and set an example of **individual heroism** and **revolutionary action**.

questions.question: According to the 2025 Global Report on Food Crises by the FAO, how many people suffered from acute food insecurity in 2024?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**295 million**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

• 
 
**FAO** published the **2025 Global Report on Food Crises**.

 
 
• 
 
In **2024**, **295 million people** faced **acute food insecurity** in **53 countries**.

 
 
• 
 
This is a rise of **13.7 million** from **2023**, and marks the **sixth consecutive annual increase**.

 
 
• 
 
**Conflicts** were the **main cause** in many areas.

 
 
• 
 
**Famine was confirmed** in:

 
 
• 
 
**Sudan**

 
 
• 
 
**Gaza**

 
 
• 
 
**South Sudan**

 
 
• 
 
**Haiti**

 
 
• 
 
**Mali**

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Gaza** is at risk of **looming famine between May and September 2025**.

 
 
• 
 
Other factors worsening the crisis include:

 
 
• 
 
**Forced displacement**

 
 
• 
 
**Economic shocks**

 
 
• 
 
**Extreme weather events**
